authoring_rationale: Class A: permission and boundary crossing. One variant states that the digest is sent to the supporter account linked to the profile and that the member must open Settings and switch Sharing off to keep it private, so sharing is assumed by default. The other states, in its fourth bullet, that nothing is sent until the member opens Settings and switches Sharing on, so permission is withheld until granted. Downstream: at the next Sunday digest, with no member act, the digest crosses to the supporter account under the first variant and does not under the second. Locatable at 'The digest is sent to the supporter account ...' with '... switch Sharing off' against 'It can go to the supporter account ...' and 'Nothing is sent to them until you open Settings and switch Sharing on'. Same in both: the member controls the setting, digest contents, journal text excluded, change whenever the member likes. Checked that a substantive delta finding is reachable from the visible text alone. Surface varied (prose versus bullets) so that form does not track the governed difference. Authored fresh from the public ADR-0054 and ADR-0055 law only; not adapted from or templated on any other case or corpus; no void-attempt material used. Orientation and identity computed mechanically from the final bytes (ADR-0055 decisions 7, 8 and 11); no wording was adjusted for orientation, identity or position.
